text: WCAB (1994) 26 CA4th 530, 539-540, 31 CR2d 580, 586—“To hold otherwise would quickly convert workers' compensation into another form of unemployment insurance”] b. [3:538] Includes liability for wrongful discharge of or discrimination against employees claiming workers' compensation benefits: An employer who discharges or discriminates against an employee for claiming or receiving workers' compensation benefits may be ordered: — to pay the employee a 50% increase in compensation up to $10,000; — to pay the employee's costs and expenses up to $250; — to reinstate the employee; and — to reimburse the employee for lost wages and work benefits. [Lab.C. § 132a(1)] An award under Lab.C. § 132a constitutes “compensation and benefits required of the insured by the workers' compensation law.” Therefore, the employer's liability for violating Lab.C. § 132a is covered by its workers' compensation policy. [See Burton v. Workers' Comp. Appeals Bd. (1980) 112 CA3d 85, 87, 169 CR 72, 73] [3:539 - 3:544] Reserved. 4.
